newsitem.title: GERMANY: German deputy speaker "Johnny" Klein dies.
newsitem.headline: German deputy speaker "Johnny" Klein dies.

text.p: Hans Klein, deputy speaker of the German parliament and one of the country's most recognisable politicians, died in Bonn on Tuesday aged 65, his party said.

The bearded Klein was a journalist and diplomat who became a familiar figure on television screens with his trademark bow tie while serving simultaneously as government spokesman and development minister in 1989 and 1990.

Klein, usually known as "Johnny", first came to prominence as chief press spokesman for the Olympic Games in his native city of Munich in 1972, when 11 Israeli athletes were killed after being kidnapped by Palestinian guerrillas.
His earlier diplomatic career had taken him all over the Middle East and Indonesia as press attache.
Since 1990 he had employed his typically wry, easy-going manner as one of four deputies to parliamentary speaker Rita Suessmuth.

Theo Waigel, finance minister and chairman of Klein's Bavarian-based Christian Social Union as well as a personal friend of Klein, said his unmistakable style and international reputation had strengthened Germany's position in the world and helped to keep its politics accessible to ordinary people.
